- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 18-day mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 5+ days, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 18-day moving average.
- Model underestimates downward trends after sentiment turns negative; if sentiment drops below 0.00, add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often dips 1–3 days after model’s peak; shift forecast peak 1–3 days earlier.
